title: Forms
objective: Read values from a form (text, numbers, checkboxes, select lists), validate them and show errors on the page
story: You're at the last stop on Planet DOM! The control tower wants the details of every pilot who's about to fly. Today you'll learn to get data from **forms** and to catch information that was entered wrong.

sections.title: The submit event and preventDefault
Reading the value in a box
sections.body:
The text inside an `input` is in its `.value` property, and it's **always text**, even if a number was typed:

```js
const raw = document.querySelector("#fuel").value; // "150"
const fuel = Number(raw);                          // 150
if (Number.isNaN(fuel)) {
  console.log("That's not a number!");
}
```

- `.value.trim()` removes spaces at the start and end: `"  Ada "` → `"Ada"`
- `Number("abc")` gives `NaN`; you can tell with `Number.isNaN(...)`.
- `Number("")` gives `0`. Don't forget to check for an empty box separately!

sections.title: Checkboxes and select lists
sections.body:
With a checkbox (`type="checkbox"`) what matters isn't the text but whether it's ticked: `.checked` gives us `true` or `false`. In a select list (`select`), `.value` is the `value` of the selected `option`:

```js
const ready = document.querySelector("#ready").checked;      // true / false
const crew = Number(document.querySelector("#crew").value);  // "3" → 3
```

tasks.title: Mission log
tasks.prompt:
When the form is submitted:

- the page must not reload (`preventDefault`),
- the mission name in the `#mission` box, with spaces trimmed, is written into `#out` like `Mission saved: Explore Mars`,
- the form is reset (`form.reset()`).
tasks.html: No mission yet.
tasks.starter:
const form = document.querySelector("#mission-form");

// listen to the submit event

tasks.title: Fuel calculator
tasks.prompt:
When the form is submitted, calculate the total fuel: the number in the `#fuel` box × the number of tanks chosen in the `#tanks` list.

- Write the result into `#out` like `Total fuel: 300 liters`.
- If the fuel isn't a number, or is 0 or less, write `Please type a valid number.`
hints: If Number.isNaN(fuel) || fuel <= 0, write the error message and leave with return.

tasks.title: Launch approval
tasks.prompt:
When the form is submitted:

- If the `#ready` checkbox is **not** ticked, write `Confirm the safety check first!` into `#out` and add the `error` class to `#out`.
- If it's ticked, write `Launch approved: crew of 3` (the number comes from the `#crew` list) and remove the `error` class.

challenge.title: Sign-up form
challenge.prompt:
Validate the sign-up form. When the form is submitted, find all the errors and add each one to the `#errors` list as a separate `<li>` (clear the list first):

- If the username (spaces trimmed) isn't between 3 and 12 letters: `The username must be 3-12 letters.`
- If the age isn't a whole number between 10 and 99: `The age must be a number between 10 and 99.`

If there are no errors, write `Signed up, Ada!` into `#out` and reset the form. If there are errors, `#out` stays empty.
hints: const errors = []; every time you find an error: errors.push("...")

project_task.title: Pilot name form
project_task.prompt:
Let's get the pilot's name before the game starts. When `#pilot-form` is submitted:

- The page must not reload.
- If the name (spaces trimmed) is empty, write `Type the pilot's name first!` into `#info` and add the `error` class.
- Otherwise put the name into the `pilotName` variable, write `Get ready, Captain Ada!` into `#info`, remove the `error` class and reset the form.
